clue.text: Tomboy gives call to study

parts.note: hoy is a shout used to attract attention, a call
a den is a private room for working, a study

explanation.surface: A boisterous girl shouts at someone to come into the study.
explanation.walkthrough: HOY is an old hailing cry; a DEN is a snug study. 'gives' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoyden is a boisterous, unladylike girl, the same idea as a tomboy.

clue.text: Moulding loves to devour a small volume

indicators.note: devouring takes something into the mouth, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so two loves are two Os
vol. is the short form of volume

explanation.surface: A bookworm sweetheart is so smitten they would eat a slim book.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Os from 'loves' swallow VOL; the 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex rounded moulding used in classical architecture.

clue.text: U.S. conscript ? English planner

explanation.surface: Two figures set side by side: an American draftee and a British planner.
explanation.definitionFit: An American conscript is a man taken in the draft, while a planner who draws designs drafts them, so both are draftsmen.

clue.text: Tamper illegally with the race issue

definitions.text: Tamper illegally with the race issue

parts.words: Tamper illegally with the race issue
parts.note: read as fixing a horse race by drugging or disabling a runner beforehand

explanation.surface: Interfering corruptly in a matter of ethnic politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race issue' sounds like a social question, but it means the result of a horse race, which crooks fix by injuring or doping a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble a racehorse is to drug or lame it so it cannot win, a crime that tampers with the outcome.

clue.text: But this premier was no hippie

definitions.text: But this premier was no hippie

parts.words: But this premier was no hippie
parts.note: a rose's fruit is its hip, so a rose fruit called a berry would not be a hip: a prime minister's name split as a rose and a berry

explanation.surface: A historic prime minister was certainly no long-haired flower child.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Rosebery was a British prime minister in the 1890s; his name splits as ROSE + BERRY, and the fruit of a rose is a hip, so a rose-berry is literally 'no hip'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Rosebery led the British government in 1894 to 1895, so he was a premier.

clue.text: An engaging occupation in retirement

parts.note: read militarily: an engagement with the enemy fought while an army is retreating

explanation.surface: A pleasant hobby for a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaging' and 'retirement' suggest a hobby for a pensioner, but they mean a battle and a retreat: troops at the back fight off pursuers while the army withdraws.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive fight by the rear of a retreating force; an engagement fought while withdrawing.

clue.text: It facilitates a frame-up that may be your look-out

definitions.text: It facilitates a frame-up that may be your look-out

parts.words: It facilitates a frame-up that may be your look-out
parts.note: read literally: a device that helps raise a window frame, the window being what you look out of

explanation.surface: Something that helps stitch up an innocent person, which is your problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frame-up' and 'your look-out' suggest a criminal set-up, but they mean lifting a window frame, and a window you look out of.
explanation.definitionFit: The cord running over a pulley in a sash window lets the sliding frame be raised and held open.

clue.text: Law of the premiership

parts.note: read as the man named Law who held the office of prime minister, not a rule of office

explanation.surface: A rule governing how a prime minister holds office.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Bonar Law was British prime minister in 1922 to 1923; 'Law' is his surname, not a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonar was the first name of the Conservative leader Bonar Law, briefly prime minister.

clue.text: Add strength to ribbon

indicators.note: the instruction to add tells you to put one word on after the other

parts.note: ribbons is an old word for the reins of a horse, so a ribbon is a rein
force is power, strength

explanation.surface: Advice to stiffen a length of ribbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ribbon' gives REIN, from the old coaching use of 'ribbons' for reins; adding FORCE (strength) to it builds the answer, and the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce something is to make it stronger by adding support.

clue.text: If the terminals get furred, these are not to blame

definitions.text: If the terminals get furred, these are not to blame

parts.words: If the terminals get furred, these are not to blame
parts.note: the terminals are read as the Earth's poles, and the furry animals living there are innocent of furring them

explanation.surface: Battery terminals have gone furry with corrosion, and these items are cleared of blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminals get furred' suggests corroded battery terminals, but the terminals are the poles of the Earth; Arctic animals have fur, yet that is not what 'furred' poles mean.
explanation.definitionFit: These large white Arctic animals live around the North Pole.

clue.text: Fain would be simple?

indicators.note: the word fain wishes to be something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eager to be thought unsophisticated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fain' means gladly; 'would be' tells you to rearrange its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif is a variant of naive, meaning artless or unsophisticated.

clue.text: Tramp's record of miles?

parts.note: read as a log kept of distance in feet, a record of miles walked

explanation.surface: The diary a vagrant keeps of distances covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a vagrant but is a verb, to walk heavily; split the answer as FOOTS + LOG and it is a record of feet travelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To footslog is to march or trudge a long way on foot, to tramp.

clue.text: Artist in estaminet calls for bottle

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as the artist is inside the bar

parts.note: an estaminet is a small French cafe or bar
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter in a French bar orders a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: An estaminet is a small French bar; 'calls for' is only a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass bottle or flask for serving wine or water at table.

clue.text: "—— of mind all passion spent" (Milton)

parts.note: a gap to fill from the closing line of Milton's Samson Agonistes

explanation.walkthrough: The last line of Milton's Samson Agonistes is 'And calm of mind, all passion spent'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the noun for peace and tranquillity that completes Milton's line.

clue.text: Blooming snake put down

parts.note: read as the Bible's staff that turned into a serpent when thrown down and later blossomed

explanation.surface: An annoying snake has been killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British swear word and 'put down' like killing an animal, but in Exodus Aaron's staff became a snake when cast down, and in Numbers it budded and bloomed; the name is also a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Aaron's staff turned into a serpent when thrown on the ground and later flowered; mullein is also called by that name.

clue.text: In broken English he's heard to say it's hard work eating ants

definitions.text: In broken English he's heard to say it's hard work eating ants

parts.words: In broken English he's heard to say it's hard work eating ants
parts.note: read as the ant-eating creature whose name, said with a dropped H in Cockney fashion, sounds like a complaint about effort

explanation.surface: A foreigner with poor English complains that eating ants is laborious.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with a dropped H, as in Cockney speech, 'hard work' comes out like the name of the African animal that lives on ants and termites.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing African mammal feeds on ants and termites with its long sticky tongue.

clue.text: Art of the plug-hole?

parts.note: read as an art movement named after the swirling of water draining away

explanation.surface: Asking whether a drain could inspire a style of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Vorticism was a British art movement of about 1914; its name comes from vortex, the whirlpool water makes going down a plug-hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Vorticism was an early twentieth-century British avant-garde art movement led by Wyndham Lewis.

clue.text: Essays Eve trick among old army girls

indicators.note: one piece sits among the letters of the other

parts.note: the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the women's branch of the British Army in the Second World War
Eve tempted Adam in Eden, so to trick like Eve is to tempt

explanation.surface: Eve plays a trick on a group of wartime army women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essays' looks like a plural noun but is a verb here, meaning tries; 'old army girls' is a standard crossword route to the wartime women's service.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to try it, so essays are tries or efforts.

clue.text: Having scallops, originated around the Arctic

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to create something is to originate it
the Arctic is the far north, abbreviated N

explanation.surface: Shellfish first came from the polar region.
explanation.walkthrough: CREATED goes around N. 'scallops' are not shellfish here but a wavy edge, as on a leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A crenated edge has rounded notches, like a scalloped border on a leaf.

clue.text: Film dance

explanation.surface: Two words, one for the cinema and one for the ballroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a spool of cinema film, and also a lively Scottish country dance.

clue.text: The boy can wait

parts.note: read as the French word for boy, which also means a waiter

explanation.surface: An adult says the child's needs can be put off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wait' means serve at table, not be patient: the French word for boy also names a waiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Garçon is French for boy and is the traditional way to call a waiter in a French cafe.

clue.text: Ozone's uncommonly good for insomnia

indicators.note: uncommonly suggests the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Breathing the ozone at the seaside is a fine cure for sleeplessness.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'Ozone's' supplies all six letters, its S included, and 'uncommonly' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A short light sleep, a nap, is just the thing for someone suffering sleeplessness.

clue.text: To excel, flout doctor's orders to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, the run of letters inside the words

explanation.surface: A patient overachieves by partly ignoring medical advice.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'flOUT DOctor's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass or do better than, the transitive sense of excel.

clue.text: Grace, the daily obliger, is a graduate

parts.note: a char or daily is a cleaning woman who obliges by coming in each day
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady named Grace has a university degree.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'daily' or char is a woman who cleans someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal charm, a gift or grace that attracts others.

clue.text: Low call to honoured companion to hang around

parts.note: a moo is the lowing call of a cow
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A soft-voiced invitation to a distinguished friend to stay on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is a cow's call, not quiet; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to loiter or wander about aimlessly.

clue.text: How David's Aunt Betsey started to go?

definitions.text: How David's Aunt Betsey started to go?

parts.words: How David's Aunt Betsey started to go?
parts.note: read as the pet name Betsey ... gave David Copperfield, which is also a gentle running pace

explanation.surface: A question about how a Dickens character set off walking.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's David Copperfield, Aunt Betsey Trotwood called David 'Trot'; to trot is also to start moving at a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot is a gait faster than a walk, how one starts to run; and the nickname Betsey gave her nephew.

clue.text: Composer of this opera had no end of a battle

parts.words: Composer of this opera had no end of a battle
parts.note: the composer's name is a famous battle of 1812 with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: An opera composer endured a never-ending struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Borodin wrote the opera; drop the end of Borodino, Napoleon's 1812 battle, and you have Borodin.
explanation.definitionFit: Borodin's opera tells of a twelfth-century Russian prince's campaign against the Polovtsians.

clue.text: A damn swear-word, lad, can get you a living

parts.note: the word damn is printed as d— in polite writing, so it is D
a vow is a solemn sworn word
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: A boy who curses discovers it earns him a parish income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swear-word' is not a curse but a VOW, a sworn promise; a 'living' is a church benefice.
explanation.definitionFit: An advowson is the right to appoint a clergyman to a church benefice, which is called a living.

clue.text: Young ladies improvising hymns around the piano

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes around the musical letter
improvising means making it up, so the letters of hymns are reworked

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Girls make up hymn tunes around the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of HYMNS goes around P, the musical marking for 'piano' (softly).
explanation.definitionFit: Nymphs are beautiful young women in mythology, and by extension young ladies.
